skill.name: opentargets-database
skill.description: Query the Open Targets Platform for target-disease associations, tractability, safety, genetics, omics evidence, and known drugs.
skill.summary: Research therapeutic targets and drug evidence with Open Targets GraphQL data.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally queries the public Open Targets Platform GraphQL API and documents official Open Targets endpoints. Most static findings are false positives from markdown backticks, biomedical identifiers, or the word success in scientific context. No prompt injection, credential access, destructive behavior, or unauthorized data exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: External network access to Open Targets is required for live queries.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the endpoint limited to the documented Open Targets API and document that user queries are sent to that public service.

remediation.issue: The helper script accepts custom GraphQL query strings.
remediation.suggestion: Advise users not to include confidential patient, proprietary, or unpublished data in query variables sent to the public API.

content.value_statement: Drug discovery teams need fast access to target, disease, and drug evidence. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code query Open Targets and interpret biomedical results.
actual_capabilities: Search Open Targets entities for genes, diseases, and drugs by name or identifier.
Retrieve target annotations including tractability, safety liabilities, genetic constraint, and associated diseases.
Get disease information with associated targets and known drugs.
Fetch target-disease evidence across genetics, pathways, literature, known drugs, and expression data.
Inspect drug details such as mechanisms, indications, trial phase, and withdrawal notices.
Guide interpretation of Open Targets scores and evidence types for target prioritization.
limitations: Requires internet access to the public Open Targets API for live queries.
Open Targets scores are ranking signals, not clinical success probabilities.
Bulk analyses should use Open Targets downloads or BigQuery instead of repeated API calls.
Scientific findings still require expert biological and clinical review.

use_cases.title: Prioritize targets for a disease program
use_cases.description: Find top associated targets, compare evidence types, and review tractability and safety signals.

use_cases.title: Validate a proposed therapeutic target
use_cases.description: Collect target annotations, disease links, known drugs, and genetic evidence before deeper review.

use_cases.title: Explore drug repurposing opportunities
use_cases.description: Review known drugs, mechanisms, clinical phases, and related disease indications for a target area.

prompt_templates.title: Find an entity identifier
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a gene, disease, or drug name and need the Open Targets identifier.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Open Targets for BRCA1 as a target and summarize the best matching identifier and name.

prompt_templates.title: Review target annotations
prompt_templates.scenario: Assess whether a gene has useful drug discovery signals.
prompt_templates.prompt: Get Open Targets information for ENSG00000157764 and summarize tractability, safety liabilities, genetic constraint, and top disease associations.

prompt_templates.title: Compare evidence for an association
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate why a target is linked to a disease.
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve evidence for ENSG00000157764 and EFO_0000249. Group the results by evidence type and explain which evidence looks strongest.

prompt_templates.title: Build a target prioritization brief
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a concise research summary for a disease program.
prompt_templates.prompt: For Alzheimer disease, identify top associated targets, known drugs, key evidence types, tractability concerns, and safety cautions. Present a ranked shortlist with caveats.

output_examples.input: Find Open Targets results for aspirin.
output_examples.output: A concise drug summary with the ChEMBL identifier, synonyms, drug type, maximum clinical phase, mechanisms of action, and disease indications.

output_examples.input: Assess BRAF as a therapeutic target.
output_examples.output: A target assessment covering approved symbol, disease associations, tractability signals, safety liabilities, known drug evidence, and interpretation cautions.

output_examples.input: Which evidence supports a target-disease association?
output: Scores and study references when available
Notes on genetic, known drug, literature, and expression support

best_practices: Start with exact Open Targets identifiers before requesting detailed evidence.
Compare multiple evidence types instead of relying on a single association score.
Use primary literature and domain review before making clinical or investment decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not treat association scores as probabilities of clinical success.
Do not send confidential patient or proprietary data to the public API.
Do not use repeated API calls for large systematic analyses when downloads or BigQuery are available.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: No. The Open Targets GraphQL API is public and does not require authentication.

faq.question: Can it analyze many targets at once?
faq.answer: It is best for exploratory queries. Large systematic analyses should use Open Targets downloads or BigQuery.

faq.question: What identifiers does it use?
faq.answer: It uses Ensembl gene IDs for targets, EFO IDs for diseases, and ChEMBL IDs for drugs.

faq.question: Can it predict whether a drug program will succeed?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes evidence and ranking signals, but clinical success requires expert review and additional data.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What data types can it retrieve?
faq.answer: It can retrieve genetics, pathways, literature, expression, animal model, somatic mutation, and known drug evidence when available.
